evidence.quote: Each deployed block evolves the state exactly under \(\dot z=-\nabla f(z)\) for elapsed time \(\tau\); it is not the implicit-Euler map \((I+\tau\nabla f)^{-1}\). A block contracts pairwise distances by a factor at most \(e^{-\tau}\) and reduces \(f\) by a factor at most \(e^{-2\tau}\). Because \(n\) identical blocks equal \(\Phi_{n\tau}\), they guarantee \(\|Z_n\|\le e^{-n\tau}\|Z_0\|\) and \(f(Z_n)\le e^{-2n\tau}f(Z_0)\). Here \(\tau\) is the continuous evolution time, not the coefficient in the proximal convention, whose quadratic term remains \(\frac12\|u-z\|^2\). For this particular flow, no convex proximal representation exists for any \(\tau>0\), so the deployment should not be described as an exact convex regularization step.
